comment: Shared cross-implementation negative-vector corpus (SEC-3). Every entry is non-canonical CBOR that BOTH the Rust qub-core decoder and the TypeScript workers/api decoder MUST reject. Each `hex` decodes to a structurally plausible CBOR value but uses a non-canonical encoding — an indefinite-length item, a non-minimal integer encoding, or trailing bytes. Consumed by crates/qub-core/tests/non_canonical_cbor_vectors.rs and workers/api/src/crypto/__tests__/non-canonical-cbor.test.ts. This file is the single source of truth: do not fork it.

vectors.name: top_level_indefinite_map
vectors.reason: indefinite-length map at the top level

vectors.name: nested_indefinite_array
vectors.reason: {"v": [_ ]} — indefinite-length array as a field value

vectors.name: nested_indefinite_map
vectors.reason: {"v": {_ }} — indefinite-length map as a field value

vectors.name: nested_indefinite_byte_string
vectors.reason: {"v": (_ )} — indefinite-length byte string as a field value

vectors.name: nested_indefinite_text_string
vectors.reason: {"v": (_ )} — indefinite-length text string as a field value

vectors.name: non_minimal_uint8
vectors.reason: {"v": 1} — value 1 encoded as a uint8 (0x18 0x01) not the canonical 0x01

vectors.name: trailing_bytes
vectors.reason: canonical empty map (0xa0) followed by a trailing 0x00 byte

vectors.name: map_keys_out_of_order
vectors.reason: {"version": 1, "body": h'78'} — keys out of canonical order ("version" (7 bytes) must not precede "body" (4 bytes)); ciborium re-encodes it byte-identically, so only an explicit decode-side key-order check rejects it
